newsitem.title: GERMANY: KLM wins Germany air cargo market share.
newsitem.headline: KLM wins Germany air cargo market share.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV looks set to win a higher share of the Germany air cargo market this year from rivals such as Lufthansa Cargo AG and Air France.

Oliver Evans, KLM sales director Central & Eastern Europe, told Reuters in an interview that the airline expected to increase its ex-Germany tonnage by about 10 percent in the March 1995-April 1996 fiscal year.
Since this was likely to be higher than general market growth and that of leading competitors, it would amount to an increased market share, industry sources noted.
Evans declined to give any absolute figures for KLM's tonnage and revenue from the German market.
But he confirmed he saw Lufthansa and Air France as the airline's main rivals in Germany.
"KLM sees itself as a major player on the German market. Among those carriers with a global network, I would say KLM is among the top three in this market," he said.
Germany was KLM's second-largest market behind the U.S. and much larger than the domestic Dutch market, he added.
"We consider Europe as our home base rather than Holland. In the German market our connections from many German cities are as advantageous as those of the national carrier," Evans said.
KLM moved the "vast majority" of its ex-Germany airfreight by scheduled truck services to Amsterdam for onward air transport, he added.

"We can gear the departure times to the needs of the German market, we can add frequencies or capacities almost instantly according to demand and that is a tremendous tool," he noted. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
